question: What is the main purpose of a carburetor in a gasoline engine?
solution:
The correct answer is __Atomising and vaporising****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A carburetor__ is an integral part of a gasoline engine used for mixing air and fuel.
 
• Its primary function is to atomise and vaporise the fuel to prepare a suitable air-fuel mixture for combustion.
 
• The air-fuel mixture must be in the correct ratio to ensure efficient engine performance.
 
• Carburetors operate on the principle of Bernoulli's theorem, where the pressure decreases as the air velocity increases.
 
• Most modern vehicles have replaced carburetors with fuel injection systems, but they are still used in certain engines and applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Igniting the fuel-air mixture:**

 
 
• This is done by the spark plug, not the carburetor.
 
 
 
• **Storing fuel for the engine:**
 
 
• This is a function of the fuel tank.
 
 
 
• **Cooling the engine:**
 
 
• Engine cooling is handled by the cooling system (radiator, coolant, etc.), not the carburetor.
